title: Code signing, provisioning and App Store distribution
summary: iOS only runs apps signed with a certificate Apple trusts. A provisioning profile ties together who signed it (certificate), which app (bundle ID), which capabilities (entitlements) and which devices may run it.
body: **In simple words:** Signing proves the app comes from you and was not modified. Provisioning says where and how it is allowed to run.

**The pieces:** **Certificate** - your identity (Development or Distribution), with a private key on your Mac or CI. **App ID / Bundle ID** - `com.shop.app`. **Entitlements** - capabilities like push, App Groups, Keychain sharing, iCloud, Associated Domains. **Provisioning profile** - certificate + app ID + entitlements (+ device list for development/ad hoc).
**Profile types:** Development (your test devices), Ad Hoc (up to 100 registered devices), App Store (TestFlight and App Store), Enterprise (in-house, separate program).

**Release path:** Archive → upload to App Store Connect → TestFlight (internal testers immediately; external testers after a short beta review) → submit for App Review → release (manual, automatic, or phased over 7 days).

**CI tips:** automatic signing for local dev; on CI use App Store Connect API keys, fastlane match or Xcode Cloud to manage certificates and profiles. Most "build failed" signing errors are a missing entitlement in the profile or an expired certificate.
**App Review:** follow the guidelines (privacy, in-app purchase rules, no hidden features); expedited review exists for critical fixes.
keyPoints: Certificate = who; bundle ID = what; entitlements = capabilities; profile = all tied together.
Profiles: development, ad hoc, App Store, enterprise.
Archive → App Store Connect → TestFlight → review → (phased) release.
Automate signing on CI (API keys, match, Xcode Cloud).
Entitlement mismatch is the most common signing error.
mistakes: Sharing a single developer's personal certificate across the team without managed storage.
Adding a capability in Xcode but not regenerating the profile on CI.
followups: **Why does push not work in a TestFlight build but works in debug?** Debug uses the sandbox APNs environment; the server must use production for TestFlight/App Store, and the profile must include the push entitlement.

**What happens when a distribution certificate expires?** Existing App Store apps keep working; you just cannot sign new builds until you create a new one (enterprise apps are different - they stop launching).
